name: Fifteen Flags and Six Republics: The Eastern Bloc Breaks
description: The end of the Soviet Union, Yugoslavia and Czechoslovakia and the birth of more than twenty new states in just a few years around 1991.

checkpoints.name: The old federations
checkpoints.note: Soviet rule and Yugoslavia hold many nations in single states. In Poland, East Germany and Czechoslovakia, Soviet-backed governments rule, with growing unrest through the 1980s.

checkpoints.name: The walls fall
checkpoints.note: The Berlin Wall opens in 1989, communist governments fall across Eastern Europe, and Germany reunites. In 1990 Lithuania becomes the first Soviet republic to declare independence.

checkpoints.name: Fifteen flags
checkpoints.note: After the failed coup of August 1991 the republics leave one by one, and the Soviet Union is dissolved in December. Slovenia and Croatia declare independence, and war breaks out in the Balkans.

checkpoints.name: Aftermath
checkpoints.note: Czechoslovakia splits peacefully while the Yugoslav wars end in Bosnia and Kosovo. Serbia and Montenegro part in 2006, and Kosovo declares independence in 2008.
